messages:
devon: Seeing intermittent decrypt failures during our EU->US DR failover. Error: AccessDeniedException on aws.kms decrypt for key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:key/abc... Anyone seen this with MRKs?

isabel: can you paste the exact error/log line?

devon: log: "AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::444455556666:assumed-role/redwood-dr-role is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111122223333:alias/my-cmk (Service: AWSKMS; Status Code: 400; Error Code: AccessDeniedException)"

priya: quick Q: are you calling Decrypt against the primary or the replica ARN? MRK behavior requires calling the key ID/ARN of the region you're targeting, right?

devon: clients are hitting alias my-cmk without region-specific ARN. During failover traffic is routed to us-east-1; looks like alias points to us-east replica but the decrypt call still resolves to eu-west arn in logs.

jamie: MRKs are weird: you can create a multi-region key with primary in eu-west and replica in us-east. The replica has a different ARN and key-id and its own key policy. IAM policies referencing the primary won't magically apply to the replica.

isabel: 2 main checks: 1) key policy on the replica must allow the cross-account role (redwood-dr-role). 2) if you're using grants, make sure they're created against the replica key (grant tokens don't replicate).

priya: also watch for Envelope Encryption client behaviour. If your envelope uses a CMK in eu-west to encrypt data key, clients must call Decrypt on that same key/ARN. If failover routes requests to replica, decryption will fail unless the replica has identical key material and policy.

devon: noted. How do we ensure our cross-account role gets access to the replica? Adding the role to the replica key policy is enough?

jamie: yes, typically update replica key policy to include the other account/principal. Example snippet:

```
{
  "Sid": "AllowRedwoodDR",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/redwood-dr-role"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:Encrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

But also ensure any IAM policy in calling account allows kms:Decrypt on that replica ARN.

isabel: if using cross-account CMKs, remember to include "kms:ViaService" condition for service calls from other regions if needed.

devon: what about rotation? We rotated primary last week and clients started failing—could that be related?

priya: rotation on MRK's primary rotates key material for primary only; replicas don't rotate automatically. You have to manually rotate replicas or recreate? (I think AWS replicates new material when you perform re-replication? double-check)

jamie: AWS supports rotating multi-region keys but there are nuances. Best practice: test rotation in staging. For immediate issues, check key metadata: aws kms describe-key --key-id <replica-arn> and check "MultiRegion" and KeyState.

devon: ran describe-key on replica: shows "KeyState":"Enabled","MultiRegion":true,"Origin":"AWS_KMS"; policies show no cross-account entry. I'll add the role.

isabel: also add CloudTrail lookup to verify which principal attempted decrypt. Example lookup: 

```
filter @message like /Decrypt/ | fields @timestamp, userIdentity.arn, eventName, resources
```

we should see which ARN failed.

ops-bot: Ticket #SEC-4312 created: Investigate MRK decrypt failures during eu->us failover. Assigned to devon, priya. :clipboard:

devon: adding the role to replica policy now, will redeploy and test. Thanks!

priya: FYI if problems persist, we can add an alias per-region and make clients target region-specific alias (alias/us-east-1/my-cmk) to avoid ambiguity.

jamie: also watch for KMS quotas and request throttling during failover; sudden burst to replica can hit limits. Add retries and exponential backoff.

devon: update: after policy change decrypts succeeded for most, but one legacy service still fails with "InvalidCiphertextException" — looks like it stored data key encrypted under old key version.

isabel: that implies you need re-encrypt or data migration for that service. We can coordinate a key-rotation-aware migration.

priya: noted, I'll open a follow-up doc with migration steps and audit log checklist.

devon: thanks all :heart:
